thesis: Institutions reward components and strategies, not diagnostic labels; empathy costs may be socially produced.
role: Test dark-trait hypothesis against inconsistent results and positive caregiving mechanisms.

ideas.statement: Partner markets and platform objectives shape reproductive opportunities before births.
Dark traits have inconsistent reproductive associations and depend on reputation, sanctions and cooperation.
Suspicion needs evidence-responsive calibration rather than blanket validation or elimination.
Reducing suffering is compatible with neurodiversity; clinical illness is not an adaptive strategy.
The quality trap can make demanding parenting prohibitively costly; shared care can change that.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Croatian sample and Serbian prisoner findings point in different directions.
Large Swedish study finds reduced fertility for most diagnosed groups, with specified exception.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: No robust general evidence establishes empathy being selected against.
Clinical paranoia is not political skepticism; polygenic associations are not diagnosis causing fertility.
Initial mating success need not become stable parenting or surviving descendants.

audit.notes: Entire assigned batch read; numbered subchapters covered; no independent citation verification.
